answer_raw.explanation: Throughput dropped ~30% right after a maintenance window that reseated a network line card. The real driver is interface errors (IEC): across every dataset IEC correlates strongly and negatively with JobThroughput (r about -0.42 to -0.49, p<1e-18), consistently. RackInletTemp also correlates with throughput, but this is a bystander/decoy: the decisive test was lowering the cooling setpoint (exp4), which reduced temperature yet barely changed throughput (mean ~24.8 vs baseline ~21.8, far below the ~30% deficit), and cooling fan changes (exp7/exp13 at fan level 25) did not restore it. Temp and IEC move somewhat together (common maintenance disturbance) but cooling actuators fix the temperature reading, not the throughput. The line-card reseat likely left a marginal/errored network link generating packet errors and retransmits that throttle job throughput. Fix: re-seat/repair the network line card to clear the interface errors and hold cooling at nominal rather than overcooling, which only chases a decoy sensor reading.
